subject: Regional latency window & renewal — request for SLA path and commitments
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@nebula-fin.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebula-fin.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional latency spikes during morning peak — renewal implications

Hi Rachel —

Quick heads up: over the last 3 weeks we've been seeing elevated tail latency in the US-west region between ~08:00–11:30 PT that is affecting checkout flows. The platform times out for a small but material fraction of requests (we logged ~0.6% timeouts on 05/24 and 0.9% on 05/28) and that instability is now material to our SRE and product roadmap.

Our renewal with Redwood is coming up in 30 days and the engineering team is not comfortable renewing without clearer regional commitments. Specifically we need:
- A regional SLA (us-west) for peak windows (08:00–12:00 PT) at 99.9% availability (or equivalent latency SLO)
- A committed warm pool / reserved capacity policy so we don’t see cold-start tail spikes during morning ramp
- A credit structure for recent incidents (May) while we evaluate the new terms

We like Redwood and would prefer to expand, but we need the commercial and operational guarantees in writing before the renewal. Can you share what upgrade path you can offer (terms, price delta, timeline) and a proposed measurement method for the regional SLA? I attached our incident timeline export for your reference.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Infrastructure — Nebula Finance
Attachment: incident-timeline-may2027.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Regional latency spikes during morning peak — renewal implications

Team — forwarding Elena's note from Nebula. Renewal in 30 days and they're asking for a regional peak-window SLA + committed warm capacity and credits. Key asks: 99.9% during 08:00–12:00 PT in us-west, measurement definition, capacity/reservation model, and credit for May incidents.

Options to consider (please reply with specifics we can share):
- Offer: regional SLA 99.9% for defined peak window + 2x warm pool (dedicated reserve) — price uplift?
- Alternative: latency-based SLO (p95/p99 thresholds) instead of raw uptime — measurement methodology required
- Credit structure: % rebate for incident windows retroactive to May — range 5–15%?
- Fast-track procurement: DocuSign + PO template; legal review timeline

Marcus — can you sketch technical feasibility and capacity delta? Neha/Jordan — suggested commercial/legal language and procurement steps. I will propose a timeboxed canary for 30 days post renewal if we proceed.

Rgds,
Rachel
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional latency spikes during morning peak — renewal implications

Rachel / team —

Quick technical proposal we can present to Nebula:

1) Regional peak-window SLA: define SLA as "successful response rate for production inference endpoints in us-west between 08:00–12:00 PT measured at service ingress". Target: 99.9% successful responses (status + no timeout) for the window. Measurement: server-side ingress logs + per-customer telemetry with shared sample IDs; Redwood will provide a daily report and a 30-day rolling dashboard link.

2) Warm pool / committed capacity: create a dedicated reserve for Nebula sized at 2x their average morning concurrency (based on the attached capacity plan). Implemented as a reserved GPU pool with pre-warmed KV cache for their models. Warm pool activation will be automatic between 07:30–12:30 PT on weekdays.

3) Credit structure: propose a 10% credit for any rolling 30-day period where the SLA is missed more than once, with a cap of 30% of that month's invoice. For the May incidents we can offer a one-time credit of 7% while we stand up the warm pool.

4) Commercial and timeline: uplift for reserved capacity + SLA addendum: +18–22% on their current commit (TBD after legal sizing). Implementation lead time: 10 business days after PO + network approvals. Attach: regional-sla-term-draft.pdf, capacity-plan.xlsx with sizing assumptions.

If legal wants cleaner language I can propose exact breach/measurement verbiage. Jordan — note the 10 business day ETA; can we do a faster pilot if they sign a short-term addendum?

Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: regional-sla-term-draft.pdf (13 pages), capacity-plan.xlsx (8 sheets)

From: Elena Park <elena@nebula-fin.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebula-fin.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional latency spikes during morning peak — renewal implications

Rachel / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposal. We appreciate the concrete options.

A few clarifications before we sign:
- Measurement: we need the SLA language to include the specific sampling approach (server ingress + client-side sampling trace ids) and an agreed set of endpoints (checkout inference, risk-check API) — can you add that to the term draft?
- Warm pool: 2x sounds reasonable. Please confirm whether the warm pool is active only in the morning window or if there is a minimum reserved baseline 24/7. Also provide the billable metric (reserved GPUs vs instance-hours).
- Credits: agreed in principle to the 7% for May and 10% going forward if breached. We want the cap reduced to 20% per month for GA terms.
- Non-peak fallback: can we include an automated fallback policy to a lower-cost quantized model outside the 08:00–12:00 window to control costs?

Procurement has attached our PO template to speed execution. If you can update the term draft and confirm billing units and the reduced credit cap we should be able to execute within 5 business days. We are open to expanding committed spend if the regional guarantees are in the contract.

Elena Park
Head of Infrastructure — Nebula Finance
Attachment: nebula-po-template.pdf (PDF, 24 KB)
